questions.q: What does load-time validation (during Load Interface File for Import) actually check?
options: Whether an account combination exists in the chart of accounts
Whether the file is structurally valid — a proper CSV with the expected column structure, with no concept of business rules
Whether a supplier is active
Whether debits equal credits for a journal batch
questions.explain: Load-time validation is purely a file-format check. It has no awareness of business content like supplier existence or balancing rules.

questions.q: Why can a file pass load-time validation with zero issues, yet still generate many import-time rejections?
options: Because load-time validation is broken
This situation never actually happens
Because import-time validation is random
Because the two layers check entirely different things — file structure versus business rules — and a well-formed file can still contain bad business content
questions.explain: A structurally valid file can still contain business-rule violations (duplicate values, mismatched totals, invalid references) that only import-time validation catches.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is a rejected row with a recorded reason actually a good outcome?
options: Because it means the whole load has failed and nothing can be done
Because rejected rows are automatically deleted and ignored
Because it leaves a trail that can be traced and fixed, compared to a row that would otherwise silently vanish with no explanation
Because it means the system is broken
questions.explain: The rejection mechanisms covered in this course (like AP_INTERFACE_REJECTIONS) exist specifically to leave a traceable record, which is far better than a silent, unexplained loss of data.

questions.q: If a load-time error occurs, what is it most likely to indicate?
options: A problem with the file itself — such as a malformed CSV or corrupted ZIP — rather than a specific row's business data
A business-rule problem with one specific row's content
A problem with the chart of accounts configuration
A problem with the ADFdi Excel add-in
questions.explain: Load-time failures relate to file structure and format issues, distinct from business-rule rejections that happen later, during import-time validation.

questions.q: What is the recommended first step when investigating why rows were rejected during an import?
options: Immediately delete the interface table
Review the process's execution report for a first read on what failed, then query the interface and rejections tables directly if more detail is needed
Reinstall the ADFdi Excel add-in
Contact the bank that sent the file
questions.explain: The execution report is the first, fastest stop for understanding rejections; querying the interface and rejections tables directly gives more precise detail when needed.
